fixes.explanation: Right there in front of everybody, Jesus heals the man so that he can speak and see. Two problems, one healing, no waiting. I think that man's first look at the crowd must have been something. Imagine being able to see and speak in the same moment.
The text never sends this man anywhere. Jesus heals him so that he can speak and see. The healing comes straight from Jesus, with no one else in between.
That's a different healing, where Jesus tells a blind man to wash in the pool of Siloam (John 9:7). Here, Jesus just heals him so that he can speak and see. The text doesn't mention any trip.

The crowds were astounded and asked, "Could this be the Son of David?" They saw a man healed so that he could speak and see, and a big question came out of their mouths. Notice it's a question, not an announcement. I think they were still picking their jaws up off the floor.

Elijah, the prophet (1 Kings 18:36), isn't who the crowds name here. They ask, "Could this be the Son of David?" That's the question that comes out of them after the healing. I think they were too astounded to read from anybody else's script.

Jesus says, "So then, they will be your judges." He asks the Pharisees by whom their own sons drive out demons, if He does it by Beelzebul. Those sons are the Pharisees' own, and Jesus puts them right in the middle of the question. I'd feel that one all the way down to my gold base.
Jesus doesn't call them followers. He says, "So then, they will be your judges." These are the Pharisees' own sons, who drive out demons too. Judges is the word He picks.
Behind isn't the word Jesus uses. He says, "He who is not with Me is against Me…" The word that fills that blank is against.

Jesus says, "…every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven." That's a heavy line. Notice how wide the first half is: every sin and blasphemy. Only this one is named as the exception.
Jesus doesn't say home. He says, "…out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks." So the words come from what fills the heart. Home isn't the source He names.

Jesus says, "…men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken." Every careless word, not just the big speeches. I talk a lot, so I'm taking that one seriously.
Rehearsed is an interesting guess, but it's not the word Jesus uses. He says, "…every careless word they have spoken." Careless is the word He names for the words men will give an account for.
